title: A protocol for identifying the binding sites of small molecules on the cystic fibrosis transmembrane conductance regulator (CFTR) protein
protocol: Transfect Human embryonic kidney (HEK) 293 cells in T75 flasks.
Seed HEK293 cells in one T75 flask.
Dilute 15 μg of cDNA in 150 μL of H2O.
Add 1,500 μL of DMEM (without FBS) + 150 μL of PolyFect to the diluted cDNA.
Incubate for 8 minutes.
Add 5,900 μL of DMEM (with FBS).
Change the DMEM media after 24 hours.
Add fresh DMEM media with 5 mM Sodium butyrate (NaB) at 37°C for 24 hours to enhance protein expression.
Trypsinize HEK293 cells (0.0025% Trypsin, 5 min at 37°C) and neutralize with HEK293 medium.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 600 × g.
Resuspend the cell pellet in 20 mL of Cell Lysis Buffer (10 mM HEPES, pH 7.2, 1 mM EDTA) plus protease inhibitors (one tablet per 50 mL buffer).
Lysate cells using a cell disruptor (10,000 psi at 4°C for 5 min).
Centrifuge the lysed solution at 1,900 rpm for 10 min at 4°C to remove unlysed cells.
Isolate crude membranes from the supernatant after centrifugation at 45,000 rpm for 60 min at 4°C.
Resuspend the crude membrane pellet in 250 μL of resuspension buffer (40 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.4, 5 mM MgCl2, and 0.1 mM EGTA) using a 18 gauge needle (∼20 times on ice).
Pass the solution through a 27-gauge needle (∼20 times on ice).
Quantify total protein concentrations in crude membranes using Nanodrop (expected concentration ∼7–9 mg/mL).
Aliquot crude membrane samples (∼20 μg in ∼20 μL) and snap freeze them in liquid nitrogen.
Store aliquoted membranes at -80°C.
Take 3 aliquots of crude membrane stocks (∼20 μL) and thaw in ice.
Add up to 50 μL of the re-suspension buffer plus cocktail of protease inhibitors (100× stock) to each aliquot.
Add DMSO to the samples.
Pipette 10 μM of VX-770 into the samples for control studies.
Pipette 0.1 μM of VX-770-Biot into the samples as a photoaffinity labeling probe stock solution in DMSO.
Place the samples on ice and minimize exposure to light for 20 minutes.
Transfer the samples to a 96 well plate (black sided, clear bottom) and keep them on ice.
Expose the samples to UV lamp at 30–50 mW cm-2 for 15 minutes on ice.
Add 100 μL of RIPA buffer plus protease inhibitor to each well after UV exposure.
Transfer the contents from each well back into a 1.5 mL microeppendorf tube.
Wash the wells twice more with another 100 μL of RIPA buffer and transfer all washes to the microeppendorf tubes (total final volume ∼350 μL).
Shake the samples in a cold room at 4°C for 20–30 minutes using a tube shaker.
Transfer monomeric avidin agarose beads to an Eppendorf tube and add 300 μL of RIPA buffer without Protease Inhibitors (PI).
Hand shake the mixture five times and centrifuge at 19,000 × g for 30 seconds.
Remove the supernatant and wash the beads twice with 300 μL of RIPA buffer plus PI.
Transfer samples to Eppendorf tubes containing washed monomeric avidin agarose beads.
Shake the samples on a tube shaker at 21°C–25°C for 1 hour.
Centrifuge the samples at 19,000 × g for 1 minute and transfer the supernatant to new 1.5 mL micro-Eppendorf tubes, keeping them in ice or cold room.
Add 250 μL of RIPA buffer plus PI to wash the agarose beads three times.
Add 350 μL of Elution buffer (ThermoFisher kit, Cat# 20227) and shake linearly at 21°C–25°C for 20 minutes.
Centrifuge the samples at 19,000 × g for 1 minute.
Transfer the supernatant to concentrator tubes with an ultracel-30 membrane (Millipore).
Centrifuge the samples in concentrator tubes at 19,000 × g for 7 minutes.
Centrifuge samples until reaching approximately 30 μL volume.
Transfer down the centrifugal filter to a new Eppendorf tube and centrifuge at 13,000 rpm for 30 seconds.
Add 6 μL of the 5× Laemmli buffer to each sample.
Analyze by SDS-PAGE on a 6% gel for full-length CFTR in running buffer at 150 V for approximately 1.5 hours.
Transfer proteins to a 0.2 μm nitrocellulose membrane at 100 V for 1 hour in transfer buffer.
Incubate the nitrocellulose membrane with 5% milk in T-PBS for 1 hour.
Cut the blot around 110 kDa into two parts: top part (130–250 kDa) and bottom part (75–110 kDa).
Incubate the top part with human NBD2-CFTR-specific murine mAb 596 at a dilution of 1:5,000 for overnight at 4°C.
Incubate the bottom part with human Calnexin-specific rabbit antibody at a dilution of 1:10,000 for overnight at 4°C.
Wash blots five times for 5 minutes each with T-PBS (Phosphate buffered saline with Tween 20).
Incubate the blots with anti-mouse and anti-rabbit secondary antibodies conjugated to HRP for 1 hour at 21°C–25°C.
Wash blots five times for 5 minutes each with T-PBS.
Develop blots with ECL using the Li-Cor Odyssey Fc in a linear range of exposure (0.5–5 min).
Stain gel by Coomassie Blue after electrophoresis.
Excise band corresponding to 130-180 kD MW from the stained gel.
Cut excised band into approximately 1 × 1 mm pieces.
Perform in-gel trypsin digestion according to standard protocol.
Analyze peptides obtained from CFTR labeled with VX-770-DIAZ by nano-LC-MS for detection and identification of modified peptides.
Destain gel pieces with alternating washes of freshly prepared 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate (ABC) and 50 mM ABC 50% MeCN until the color is removed.
Remove solvent after the last wash with 50 mM ABC 50% MeCN.
Dry gel pieces under vacuum in SpeedVac for 30 min–1 h.
Prepare trypsin solution in 50 mM ABC, at least equal to the gel band volume.
Add trypsin solution to dried gel pieces and allow it to soak in with an enzyme:protein ratio of 1:10 to 1:5.
Incubate gel pieces 14–16 h at 37°C with orbital shaking at 450 rpm in Thermomixer.
Extract peptides from the gel by three changes of gel band volume 0.1% formic acid (FA).
Perform one extraction each with 25%, 50%, and 75% MeCN in 0.1% FA.
Dry peptide solution under vacuum in SpeedVac.
Reconstitute dried peptide solution in 0.1% FA.
Desalt the reconstituted peptides using C18 ZipTip.
Elute from the ZipTip into an autosampler vial glass insert supplemented with an equal volume of 0.1% FA and dry briefly under vacuum to approximately 20% of the original volume.
Load the glass insert containing trypsin digest into a vial for LC-MS analysis.
Perform Nano-LC-MS analysis using an Easy-nLCTM 1200 System coupled to a Q Exactive Plus mass spectrometer.
Pre-concentrate peptides on an AcclaimTMPepMapTM 100 C18 pre-column.
Separate peptides on an AcclaimTM PepMapTM 100 C18 main column using a binary gradient of buffer A and B at a flow rate of 300 nL/min.
Acquire full MS scans in positive mode from m/z 350 to 1,500 with a resolution of 70,000.
Isolate the 15 most intense precursor ions for fragmentation using normalized higher-energy collisional dissociation energy.
Acquire MS/MS spectra at a resolution of 17,500.
